Hello! I am always interested in talking with people who have different opinions from my own - I think that is the best way of understanding other people.

I can only speak to my own experience, which has led me (a straight person) to be pretty into gay rights, but I am also interested to hear different sides of it. For instance, a friend's husband doesn't believe gay people exist, and I have always been interested to try to understand this opinion, but I've never quite been able to wrap my head around it. (The best explanation he came up with once, was something like "the default option would be for everyone to be gay, but religion and the need to reproduce mean that 'righteous' people subvert their instincts." They are Catholic, and I don't know what to think about his sexuality.)

The experiences that led me to be really into gay rights were growing up 30 years ago in a neighborhood with a gay family and a lesbian family, and seeing how their families suffered in small ways, because there was not a gay acceptance movement. They were my neighbors, nice normal people with kids. (The ladies had each had one pregnancy; the men had gotten custody of the 2 children one of them had had when married to a woman.) One of the women had been kicked out of a hospital room when her partner's mom was sick, because "she wasn't family," the kids of the guys struggled with accepting their dad's relationship with a man, and got bullied at school. They got screwed at tax time, people would call them epithets in the course of the day, etc.

Then I went to college, and met tons of gay and lesbian kids, many of whom suffered (even in the 2000's) because their parents were not ok with them being gay. So, to me it just seemed like an unnecessary way for people to be suffering, and if I can be part of that going away, that feels good. To me it feels like the area of human rights advancement that has the most momentum right now, and so has the most likelihood of succeeding/making progress.

Also, for me this is much different than drug addiction, because drug addicts hurt plenty of people, depending on the drug. Marijuana is pretty safe to use, but historically users have funded drug cartels responsible for thousands of deaths (fortunately now the US-grown market is taking a bite out of that). Heroin has such a pull as to lead addicts to lie to and steal from their friends and family members, and can easily be fatal in overdose. etc.

I was in a party playing... Rifts, I think? It was a sci-fi game in any case. Apologies if this is a bit rambly, and I'm a little fuzzy on the details since it happened a while ago so there may be some minor things I got wrong. We refer to this story in our group as 'The time we blew up the death star,' but in reality it was an unrelated doom-ship. It was our first time playing the system, so we were a group of fresh characters. This all occoured on the first session.

The basic scenario was that we were to investigate a derelect spaceship and find a machine capable of creating wormholes to anywhere in the galaxy. Afterwards, an enormous, Death Star-esque enemy ship would force us to give it up, and this would set up the first arc.

After fighting off some alien beasts in the derelect spaceship, we found the device locked in a lead box. Afterwards, we were forced to a nearby asteroid by the enemy ships and were contacted by the captain of this massive ship to give up as planned, but our captain had other plans. He has the mechanic to examine the device... Basically, it absorbs energy from the surrounding area and thus does not need any active power source. However, this takes a city's worth of power almost an hour to do anything and requires electricty. So there's no chance we can gate out with this thing on an asteroid. We think about it, and he commands the mechanic to mess withthe device. He has everyone get in spacesuits, and turns on communicators. He removes the device from the ship and places it on him.

The capitol ship arrives, and it's this enormous machine so large that it swallows the entire asteroid we're on. The crew are humanoid bug-creatures about 8 feet tall, and there's an army in here so everyone is on-edge because these guys are capable of murdering everyone on board with little effort. They board us armed, and the big bad evil guy shows himself. Our captain denies having anything of value and even being on the derelect ship, while some of our crew hides aboard our ship. The enemy commander becomes irate, and 'escorts' our captain and the crew that isn't hiding inside his ship while his crew begins combing our ship.

The commander brings us to his quarters in the middle of the ship, and explains that it is... Shall we say, a very good idea to give up the item. He's in an enemy capitol ship, surrounded by enemies, and looking at a massive insect man. He explains how we stands no chance... Our mechanic had activated the device already and set it to start going after about 15 minutes and had set the siphoning to the maximum possible. At first, the enemy commander doesn't notice but after a few minutes he's alerted to massive power failures everywhere as this device siphons power from everywhere on this kilometers-big ship. The enemies around us have any energy weapons fail. Life support goes down in the hangar that our ship is docked in, and the bug-creature's weapons go down because they're energy-based. The commander is furious, and then our captain explains how they now hold the cards while the rest of us are convinced this guy is about to murder us. I don't recall his exact words, but he basically stalls this commander as the guy slowly realizes that we're going to defeat his entire army.

He explains everything we know about the device. That the wormhole opens in an instant, and will tear his ship in two as one half is instantly transported to the planet coordinates set in the device and the other half will crumple apart as this nonfunctional ship is pulled into the wormhole. He explains how all his major weapons are offline, and how his ship is now on reserve power and his crew's guns are wothless and will be for a while. He explains how he set it in such a way that stopping the device at this point is impossible - which may have been a bluff. Then, the device goes off, and this gigantic ship is torn into bits as our crew takes cover.

The area around the captain is sucked through a wormhole, and the rest of the ship is torn apart. As the 'half' the wormhole generated on was interior, the remaining parts of the ship were essentially sucked into this hole inside-out. Further, a ship of this size utilized multiple nuclear power sources, which mostly exploded because of this wormhole turning them inside-out and blew major portions of the ship apart. The entire thing was reduced to scrap in an instant... However, our ship on the outer-lip in the hangar was still in one piece as it was a whole, solid machine, and our crew was fine. Meanwhile, those of us in this interior room with the captain and the surrounding area activated our space suits as the air was sucked from the wreckage.

We warped in a bit aways from a planet, and were pulled toward it. The relatively solid portion of wreckage sheltered us as we entered the atmosphere, and our crew in the ship essentially just tried to glide themselves down as best they could on little power. Our entire crew survived, while the enemies were reduced from at least several thousand to about a dozen knocked-out guys with nonfunctional weapons who managed to survive this experience only because of their superior alien endurance.

The DM was pretty annoyed that his giant story arc was finished in a single session, but it was so cool that everyone just sort of agreed that it was for the best.

Time to retell one of my favourite incidents! This happened a couple of years ago, so my memory is fuzzy on some of the details.
In one of my groups we usually play a homebrew Sci-Fi RPG that is fairly deadly for PCs. We’re roleplay heavy and it’s not uncommon for PCs to violently oppose each other with lethal force when ideas and ideals clash. Usually at least one PC dies in each adventure. Each adventure usually takes about a year real-time and this incident happened at the start of our 5th adventure. At the time amongst our 5 players, only 2 of the original 5 PCs were left, so there were 3 "new" faces. My PC and a close RL friends PC were the only original survivors. Him because his character was very paranoid and scared and his usual battle tactics was to hide. My character was more aggressive and had previously lost both arms and a leg (now replaced with cybernetics) due to various laserblasts, explosions, crazy robot AIs and nasty aliens.
The group consisted of 1, me, the cybernetically enhanced technician; 2, my friend the paranoid scared guy; 3, the mad scientist doctor; 4, the (former military) pilot and owner of our spaceship; 5, some guy I can’t remember; 6, NPC Janitor (because cleaning is for losers).
Anyway, during our journey, the doctor had the bright idea to cook up a nice antipsychotic drug to cure my friend of his paranoia and make him more useful to the group. Unfortunately for us, he rolled a critical failure when cooking up the drug.
My friends PC had, unbeknownst to us, a psychotic break. He became even more paranoid, was convinced we were all plotting against him, started hearing voices and became very aggressive. Not a good combination. Anyway, we were in our spaceship on route to somewhere where we had a mission to complete. I forget the details for reasons that will soon become clear. During transit my friends PC became convinced our janitor on the ship, a completely innocent NPC, was out to get him, so he killed him and threw him out the airlock.
As we arrived at our destination, the murder was discovered and some semi-violent confrontations took place. In the end, we managed to calm down our psychotic killer friend (or so we thought), and now the doctor realized his antipsychotic might not have worked as intended. We had no time to fix it right at that moment and didn't feel safe bringing him along on our short mission, so we left him on the ship and went off to complete the first step in what was supposed to have become a long epic journey.
Hours later as we triumphantly returned to the ship, we notice something is not right. We have to force our way into the ship, it's completely dark and there is no power. As the groups technician I go to investigate the drivecore (basically a nuclear reactor) so see what's up. Turns out, it's completely demolished and I receive a nice healthy dose of radiation. Well, there's your problem. Our psychotic killer has destroyed our ships power source. Our pilot and owner of the ship becomes understandably upset and charges off into the ship to find our friend and take him out. Unfortunately, our friend has boobytrapped the ship and as he opens a door an explosion tears him in half. Moments later, another casualty as a plasma-blast tears a big wide hole in the stomach of our 4th PC.
Me and our doctor carefully search the rest of the ship but can't find our friend. We decide the ship is lost and exit. As we do, we notice our psychotic friend in the distance, attempting to flee the scene. We pursue him and stumble upon another spaceship with crew. Our psychotic friend is trying to barter for passage away when we interrupt him. We try to reason with him to convince him to come peacefully.
